name: Kanyamazane

queries.query: Kanyamazane South Africa official cadastral parcel map GIS land registry
queries.result: Found the first-party Chief Surveyor-General cadastral data service and the City of Mbombela municipality. The national service documents spatial cadastral data and a public ArcGIS service with polygon layers; the municipality identifies Kanyamazane within its jurisdiction and has Spatial Planning and GIS functions. No local municipal parcel API was exposed by the municipality website.

queries.language: siSwati (local language; English is also official)
queries.query: Kanyamazane eSwatini siSwati cadastre map parcels official
queries.result: No distinct siSwati-language local cadastral viewer was found. Results led back to South African first-party cadastral and City of Mbombela sources; Kanyamazane is in South Africa, not Eswatini. The South African official cadastral service remains the relevant source route.

officialSources.operator: Chief Surveyor-General / Department of Land Reform and Rural Development, South Africa; published through the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment portal
officialSources.evidence: Service metadata identifies a national cadastral layer, names the Chief Surveyor General as custodian, and exposes polygon layers Parent Farm, Farm Portions, Erven, Holdings and Public Places.
Municipal first-party site identifies the City of Mbombela and provides local services. Its official 2026/27 IDP identifies Kanyamazane as an urban area within the municipality.
Municipal organisational structure explicitly includes Spatial planning and GIS under City planning and development.

requestsAndEndpointChecks.summary: Verified-TLS ArcGIS service metadata returned five polygon-capable layers; service extent covers South Africa.
Erven layer metadata returned polygon geometry, native fields including ID, PRCL_KEY and OBJECTID, and layer CRS WKID 4148. No unsafe owner/contact/titleholder fields were requested.

Bounded anonymous GeoJSON envelope queries around the unchanged WUP point, with returnGeometry=true, outFields=ID, inSR=4326, outSR=4326 and resultRecordCount=3, returned zero features for each tested layer. This is an extent/query result only and is not evidence of citywide absence.
Separate first-party environmental screening cadastre metadata route timed out after 25 seconds; no retry with altered TLS or bypass was attempted.
Bounded point query route could not be completed; no geometry or absence conclusion was drawn.

fieldMapping.native identity: ID is the source identity field exposed by the cadastral layer; OBJECTID is retained only as a fallback schema observation. PRCL_KEY and parcel-number fields were not promoted as a composite identity.
fieldMapping.geometry: ArcGIS polygon Shape returned by the service when a feature is found.
fieldMapping.crs: Layer metadata reports WKID 4148; query output was requested in EPSG:4326 for GeoJSON compatibility, but no feature was returned to validate transformation.

coverageAssessment.claimedScope: National Chief Surveyor-General cadastral layer with polygon layers covering South Africa; Kanyamazane is within the City of Mbombela municipal jurisdiction.
coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: National service schema, polygon layers, CRS metadata and anonymous query capability were verified. Local Kanyamazane feature coverage was not verified because all bounded queries returned zero features.
coverageAssessment.targetPointHitInterpretation: No exact-point hit was obtained. The bounded query miss and the separate timeout are not evidence of citywide parcel absence; the WUP point is preserved unchanged.

remainingUncertainty: The national public service is a credible cadastral source and exposes polygon layers, but the tested Kanyamazane extent returned no features. The exact cause could be source coverage, target-point placement, service filtering, or query behavior. A serial reviewer must independently qualify local feature coverage, stable parcel identity, CRS transformation, and adapter suitability.
nextStep: Serial reviewer should inspect the current official viewer/configuration and test a bounded Kanyamazane map extent or known municipal cadastral extent independently before considering any adapter admission.
